question: How did criterion 2 get its final form?

revisions.statement: Selectivity (real - control) at the best layer
Selectivity (real - control) at the best layer

revisions.threshold: control's max balanced accuracy over layers does not exceed the 95th percentile of 10,000 redrawn mappings
revisions.note: A leak bound, not a selectivity floor: under a type-disjoint split the control task's ceiling is chance. Drafted as 0.50 ± 0.03 (b9c861b); replaced before the push because ±0.03 fires 59–80% of the time with no leak (61bf29e).

answer:
Criterion 2 went through three registered revisions.

**Revision 1** (commit 12a0349, 2026-08-22) defined it as selectivity (real minus control) at the best layer, with a threshold of ≥ 0.10 [crit-rev1-2].

**Revision 2** (commit c7323d0, same day) kept the statement but marked the ≥ 0.10 threshold as "provisional" [crit-rev2-2].

**Revision 3** (commit cb09c9d, 2026-09-26) replaced it with a different kind of criterion: "Control task shows no leak." It passes if the control's maximum balanced accuracy over layers does not exceed the 95th percentile of 10,000 redrawn mappings [crit-rev3-2]. It cites Hewitt & Liang 2019, §2.3 [paper-hewitt-liang].

The note explains the change. It is now a leak bound rather than a selectivity floor, because under a type-disjoint split the control task's ceiling is chance [crit-rev3-2]. An intermediate draft set the threshold at 0.50 ± 0.03 (commit b9c861b). That draft was replaced before the push, because a ±0.03 band fires 59–80% of the time even when there is no leak (commit 61bf29e) [crit-rev3-2]. This draft appears only in the note and has no criterion row of its own.

The rows do not say why revision 2 marked the threshold provisional.
